summary:
OrbitCare is a web-based health monitoring dashboard for astronauts on long-duration space missions. It shows real-time telemetry for each crew member: heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO₂), body temperature, radiation dose rate, cumulative radiation dose, and sleep. Vitals are shown as live tiles and charts, with alert limits marked.

It addresses the challenge by automatically flagging warning and critical conditions, such as low SpO₂, abnormal heart rate, or elevated radiation, and by generating a plain-language health summary for each astronaut. A mission-day slider models how cumulative radiation and fatigue change over time, and built-in scenarios (solar particle event, cabin CO₂ spike) demonstrate how the system responds to emergencies.

This matters because crews on deep-space missions will be far from Earth, with communication delays and limited medical support. Early detection and clear, autonomous health insights can help crews and ground teams act quickly. The prototype uses simulated data and can be extended to real sensor inputs.
details:
OrbitCare is a browser-based dashboard that monitors the health of four simulated crew members. A JavaScript telemetry simulator generates heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO₂), body temperature, radiation dose rate, cumulative dose, and sleep estimates every second. Each reading is checked against warning and critical limits. Out-of-range values trigger entries in a live alert log, and a rule-based engine writes a plain-language health summary for the selected astronaut. Live charts show heart rate, SpO₂, and radiation, each with its alert limit marked. A mission-day slider models how cumulative radiation and fatigue change over a 180-day mission. Two demo buttons, a solar particle event and a cabin CO₂ spike, trigger emergency scenarios.

Benefits
Crews and ground teams see the whole crew’s status at a glance. Problems are flagged early and in plain language, without needing an expert to read raw numbers.

Intended impact
On deep-space missions, communication delays and limited medical support mean crews must manage health autonomously. OrbitCare shows how automated monitoring and alerts could support faster, safer decisions. The prototype can be extended to real wearable sensor data.

Tools and technologies
HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Chart.js for charts. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, with the source on GitHub. No special hardware is needed. The code and slides were developed with help from an AI assistant (Claude), and the slides were presented through Google Drive.

Creativity
Instead of only displaying numbers, it combines vitals, radiation exposure, and fatigue in one view and lets you test emergencies interactively. The mission-day slider shows long-duration effects, and the auto-generated summaries make the data easy to act on.

Factors considered

  • Space-specific risks such as radiation exposure, cabin air quality, and sleep disruption
  • Communication delay and crew autonomy
  • Clear thresholds that avoid both missed alerts and alert fatigue
  • Accessibility, with readable text, status shown by more than color, and a layout that works on phones
  • Simplicity, so it runs in any browser with no install
